summary: Monolith Laravel on DigitalOcean App Platform with DigitalOcean Managed PostgreSQL as the database; front end: React + Vite, React Native.

architecture_rationale.text: One deployable Laravel app: 3 engineer(s) and scale level L3 do not justify splitting services. Microservices rejected: 3 engineer(s) cannot absorb their operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Web: A client-rendered app behind login needs no server rendering. Fit for this project: strong performance, which you rated 5/5; well suited to gaming projects; strong time to market, which you rated 4/5; React on the web and React Native on mobile share skills, hooks and business-logic code. Mobile: Builds Android and iOS apps from one TypeScript/JavaScript codebase. Fit for this project: strong time to market, which you rated 4/5; strong performance, which you rated 5/5.

alternatives.why_not: Close runner-up: the team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript; the chosen option wins on project.type (well suited to gaming projects).
Close runner-up: the team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript; the chosen option wins on priorities.performance (strong performance, which you rated 5/5).

tradeoffs: Client-rendered: no SEO for public pages.
The team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript.
JS runtime adds memory overhead on very low-end phones.
Some native modules need a development build.

backend.justification: Batteries-included PHP framework with queues and auth. Fit for this project: team.languages includes PHP; strong time to market, which you rated 4/5; built-in authentication; real-time needs an add-on (Channels).

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the team would have to learn C#; the chosen option wins on team.languages (team.languages includes PHP).

alternatives.choice: Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage + Realtime + Edge Functions)
alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the team would have to learn JavaScript/TypeScript; the chosen option wins on team.languages (team.languages includes PHP).

tradeoffs: Long-lived WebSockets run in Laravel Reverb, a separate first-party process.
Per-request overhead is tight for p95=150ms.

database.justification: ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Fit for this project: strong performance, which you rated 5/5; strong time to market, which you rated 4/5.

alternatives.why_not: Close runner-up: proprietary API increases lock-in; learning curve 4/5 for a intermediate team.

alternatives.choice: Amazon RDS for MySQL (us-east-1 N. Virginia)
alternatives.why_not: Close runner-up: it fits the rest of the stack less well.

tradeoffs: Horizontal write scaling needs partitioning, read replicas or Citus.

hosting.justification: Simple PaaS with managed Postgres and regions in India, Europe and the US. Fit for this project: strong time to market, which you rated 4/5; strong performance, which you rated 5/5.

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: it scores lower once team skills, priorities and the other layers are combined.
Close runner-up: it fits the rest of the stack less well.

tradeoffs: Fewer managed services than AWS/GCP/Azure (no managed search or ML).

supporting.justification: Uses the backend framework's maintained auth library, so user data stays in your own database.
tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.choice: Nakama (open-source game server: matchmaking, realtime, leaderboards)
supporting.justification: Matches need an authoritative server that owns game state, matchmaking and per-room broadcast at low latency for 4000 concurrent players; leaderboards live in the database/Redis sorted sets.

alternatives.why_not: You would rebuild rooms, matchmaking and reconnection logic.
Managed and proven, but per-CCU pricing and vendor lock-in.

tradeoffs: Long-lived connections must be drained on deploys; size Redis pub/sub for peak fan-out.

supporting.justification: Caches hot reads and sessions to hold p95=150ms, and carries pub/sub for real-time fan-out.

alternatives.why_not: No pub/sub or persistence, so it cannot double as a broker.
Every read hits the database at peak.

tradeoffs: Another stateful component to size and monitor.

supporting.justification: Moves slow or retry-prone work (background jobs) off the request path so p95 stays low and failures retry safely.

alternatives.why_not: Event-streaming platform: heavy to run for job queues at this scale.

tradeoffs: Jobs must be idempotent; monitor the dead-letter queue.

supporting.justification: Free push delivery to Android for messages that arrive while the app is closed.

alternatives.why_not: Costs per message and DLT templates.

tradeoffs: Notification payloads must not contain sensitive data.

supporting.choice: GitHub Actions + Expo EAS (Build, Submit, Update)
supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team. EAS builds signed Android/iOS binaries in the cloud, submits them to the stores and ships JavaScript-only fixes over the air.
Free Developer plan catches errors in the backend and mobile apps with stack traces.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.

assumptions: Scale level L3: ~80000 users, ~4000 peak concurrent, ~800 req/s at peak, ~156.2 GB stored
Upper bound capped at ~3x the lower bound: components do not all reach their peak tier in the same month
List prices for the smallest production tier that fits; no reserved-instance or startup credits; excludes domains, app-store fees and payment-gateway transaction fees

warnings.message: The low estimate ($316) fits the $400 budget, but growth to the high estimate ($998) would be more than double it; set billing alerts and revisit sizing.
The web choice (React + Vite (SPA)) needs JavaScript/TypeScript, which the team does not list; budget ramp-up time or a hire. It still scored best once constraints and other priorities were weighed.

The mobile choice (React Native (Expo)) needs JavaScript/TypeScript, which the team does not list; budget ramp-up time or a hire. It still scored best once constraints and other priorities were weighed.
